name: vscode-tslaws
description: tsc-laws for VS Code: law failures show live on the law and on the code it exercises, with CodeLens, Test Explorer and commands

scripts.test: node --test test/grammar.test.mjs test/find-laws.test.mjs test/parse-report.test.mjs test/summary.test.mjs test/command.test.mjs test/model.test.mjs test/ranges.test.mjs test/format.test.mjs test/diagnostics.test.mjs test/plan.test.mjs test/settings.test.mjs test/scheduler.test.mjs test/runner.test.mjs test/shadow.test.mjs test/host.test.mjs test/extension.test.mjs test/real-cli.test.mjs

commands.title: tslaws: Check laws in this file
tslaws: Accept (types the command in a terminal; you press Enter)
tslaws: Show the laws that reach this function
tslaws: Go to the code the law exercises

enumDescriptions: Run the laws that cover a TypeScript file when it is saved (default: a check takes a few seconds, because it compiles and proves).
Run after you stop typing, on the text of the open buffers (a copy under .tslaws/shadow; your files are not written).
Run only when you ask: the commands, a CodeLens or the Testing view.
tslaws.run.description: When to run the laws that cover the file you changed. Only those laws run: the ones that reach the file, else the laws file beside it, else all.

tslaws.runOnSave.deprecationMessage: Use tslaws.run. false means "manual", true means "onSave"; this setting only counts while tslaws.run is not set.

tslaws.debounceMs.description: How long to wait after the last change before running. A newer change stops a run that is going.

tslaws.runOnOpen.description: Run every law once when the folder opens, so failures show before the first edit.

tslaws.inlineCounterexample.description: Show the counterexample after the failing line, on the law and on the function it exercises.

tslaws.executable.description: Path of tslaws.js or a native tslaws executable (.cmd/.bat shims are refused). Empty uses the workspace's node_modules/tslaws. Machine setting: a workspace cannot set it.

tslaws.args.description: Extra arguments appended to every tslaws invocation, for example ["--compiler", "path/to/tsc"].

untrustedWorkspaces.description: tslaws runs the workspace's code (the laws and the code they check), so it does not run in an untrusted workspace.
